html:
Reggae is a style of music that began in Jamaica in the late 1960s. Its sound is a slow, heavy bass line and a guitar or piano chop on the off beat.

It grew out of ska, the fast dance music of Jamaican independence in the early 1960s, through the slower rocksteady. "Do the Reggay" by Toots and the Maytals in 1968 is often named as the first song to use the word. Big street sound systems spread new records, and producers such as Lee "Scratch" Perry made reggae's offshoot, dub, by remixing tracks into echoing instrumentals.

Reggae spoke for the poor of Kingston. Many singers were followers of Rastafari, and songs dealt with "Babylon", Africa, protest and faith.

  • Jimmy Cliff's film The Harder They Come (1972) brought it to new audiences.
  • Bob Marley made it a global sound in the 1970s.
  • Caribbean migrants of the Windrush generation made Britain a second home for it.

It shaped later music around the world. Jamaican sound system culture, carried to New York, helped give birth to hip hop. UNESCO listed reggae as world heritage in 2018.
sum: Reggae is a style of music that began in Jamaica in the late 1960s. Its sound is a slow, heavy bass line and a guitar or piano chop on the off beat.
